cover_crop: any (legume and non-legume, winter and summer)
metric: primary crop yield change (all crops pooled: rice, maize, wheat, others)
quote: The average LnR was 0.092, which means that CCs significantly (p < 0.001) increased the primary crop yield by 9.7 ± 3.7 % across the entire country (n = 442).
note: Pooled across all primary crops; not corn-specific. Unweighted analysis.

quote: The yields of rice, rice*, maize and other crops increased by 16.0 ± 3.0 %, 19.9 ± 3.8 %, 27.2 ± 9.9 % and 7.9 ± 6.3 %, respectively following winter legume CCs (Fig. 7a).
note: Maize-specific subgroup; n per category only shown in Fig. 7 (not in text). No maize estimate reported for winter non-legume or summer legume CCs. Soybean not analysed in this paper.

comparison: cover crop vs. fallow, at 0 kg N/ha (declining to 18.5% at 100 kg N/ha)
metric: primary crop yield change vs. N fertilizer input (all crops)
quote: The effect of CCs on primary crop yield decreased when N fertilizer increased from 0 kg/ha to 100 N kg/ha: from 23.0–18.5% with winter legume CCs, from 14.0–9.6% with winter non-legume CCs, and from 8.6 to 4.6 % with summer legume CCs (Fig. 8a).
note: Moderator result (N input) across all primary crops; same sentence gives 14.0->9.6% for winter non-legume and 8.6->4.6% for summer legume CCs.
